If the dryer keeps running and won’t shut off:

1. Turn it off and unplug it (or switch off the breaker).
• For a gas dryer, also turn off the gas supply if you smell gas or it is overheating.
2. Clean the lint filter and check the vent hose/outside vent for blockage. Poor airflow can cause overheating and odd cycling behavior.
3. Check whether a feature such as “Wrinkle Prevent,” “Extended Tumble,” or “Cool Down” is selected. These can keep the drum turning after the main cycle.
4. Test the behavior:
• Runs even when set to Off / keeps running with the door open: likely a stuck relay, faulty control board, or timer. Leave it unplugged and arrange repair.
• Only fails to stop on Sensor/Auto Dry: clean the two metal moisture-sensor bars inside the drum with rubbing alcohol. A faulty moisture sensor or airflow issue is also possible.
• Fails to stop on Timed Dry too: likely the timer or electronic control board.

Don’t leave it running unattended, especially if it gets unusually hot, smells burnt, or the drum continues with the door open.
its not running all the time, only after the display says End the drum turns a bit every couple of minutes. it stops when i open the door

That sounds like the dryer’s Wrinkle Prevent / Anti-Crease / Extended Tumble feature. It is usually normal.

After the display says End, the dryer periodically tumbles the load for a few seconds or minutes to reduce wrinkles. Opening the door cancels it, which matches what you’re seeing.

Look for a button or setting labeled something like:

• Wrinkle Prevent
• Extended Tumble
• Anti-Crease
• Wrinkle Guard
• Post-Cycle Care
• Less Iron

Turn that option off before starting the next cycle if you don’t want the occasional tumbling. Depending on the model, it may continue for anywhere from about 30 minutes to a few hours after the cycle ends.

If it continues doing this for an unusually long time, or it tumbles continuously rather than intermittently, check the manual/model number or have the control panel checked.
